evidence_text: A common example of a cost of financial distress is bankruptcy costs. These direct costs include auditors' fees, legal fees, management fees and other payments.

Cost of financial distress can occur even if bankruptcy is avoided (indirect costs). Another source of indirect costs of financial distress are higher costs of capital as usually banks increase the interest rates if a state of financial distress occurs.

Another source of indirect costs of financial distress are higher costs of capital as usually banks increase the interest rates if a state of financial distress occurs. Banks increase the interest rates if a state of financial distress occurs.
mechanism: Financial distress leads banks to perceive higher risk, prompting them to increase interest rates to compensate for the increased risk.

evidence_text: Financial distress in companies requires management attention. Financial distress in companies might lead to reduced attention on the operations of the company.
mechanism: Management attention is a limited resource, and when financial distress requires more of it, less is available for operations.
